newsitem.title: USA: HSBC economist sees weaker U.S. dollar - Barron's.
newsitem.headline: HSBC economist sees weaker U.S. dollar - Barron's.

text.p: Ian Shepherdson, chief U.S. economist at HSBC Markets, expects the U.S. dollar to fall and interest rates to rise in 1997, Barron's said.
Shepherdson told the financial weekly that he would not be surprised by a Clinton administration effort to drive the dollar lower while the Japanese push for a stronger yen.

The result of this monetary maneuvering would be a quick sell-off in U.S. Treasury securities by the Japanese, since they would not want to be holding dollar-denominated assets in a falling market, he told Barron's.
"There is a very definite risk that interest rates will spike in the first several months of next year," Shepherdson told the paper.

Shepherdson told the paper that he expects inflation hawks to pressure Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan to raise interest rates because of anticipated strong retail sales for November and December and strong home sales early next year.
Greenspan, however, is expected to resist because export numbers continue to look weak and he expects higher bond yields to slow down economic activity, Shepherdson told the paper.
